checks_run.procedure: Judge whether reading the stored column under the advisory lock and FOR UPDATE keeps the intent of 0101's operational_exception_guard, with no lost or double-counted occurrence.
checks_run.command: Code read of exceptions.ts:688-790, kit.ts raiseOperationalExceptionTwin, migration 0101 lines 212-220; runs in logs 53 and 54
checks_run.expected: Monotone last_occurred_at; count exactly +1 per occurrence; no rejected capture under concurrency.
checks_run.actual: Sound. Both raisers take pg_advisory_xact_lock(operationalExceptionUpsert, hashtext(key)) and then SELECT ... FOR UPDATE of the active row. In READ COMMITTED that statement sees the latest committed version after the lock, so current.occurrence_count and current.version are current. The UPDATE is guarded by 'version = current.version' with executeTakeFirstOrThrow, so a stale count can never be written silently. greatest(now(), operational_exception.last_occurred_at) reads the column in SQL at microsecond precision, so the value is never below the stored one, and the 0101 guard's 'NEW.last_occurred_at < OLD.last_occurred_at' never fires. The guard allows equality, which happens when an occurrence's transaction started earlier. Count +1 per raise under the lock means no occurrence is lost or counted twice. A resolve that commits first makes the FOR UPDATE re-check fail 'status in active', so the next failure opens a new row, as ADR-0053 states. Runs: QA round-5 probe 8/8 and 9/9 in all 10 bursts on the candidate (log 54); the BE-Z8 test 7/7; mutant M4 fails all of them (log 53). One consequence, not a defect: such an occurrence's history row can carry the same occurred_at as the previous one.
